name: Codebase
description: One codebase tracked in version control, many deploys. Every service has exactly one codebase; multiple environments are deployed from the same repo.

name: Dependencies
description: Explicitly declare and isolate dependencies. A service never relies on implicit system-wide packages; all dependencies are declared in a manifest.

name: Config
description: Store config in the environment. Everything that varies between deploys (credentials, resource handles) is stored in env vars, not in code.

name: Backing Services
description: Treat backing services as attached resources. Databases, queues, caches are bound via URL/credentials and are swappable without code changes.

name: Build / Release / Run
description: Strictly separate build and run stages. The build stage creates an immutable artifact; release combines it with config; run executes it.

name: Processes
description: Execute the app as one or more stateless processes. Processes share nothing; any persistent state lives in a backing service.

name: Port Binding
description: Export services via port binding. The service is self-contained and exposes its HTTP interface by binding to a port, not via an external web server.

name: Concurrency
description: Scale out via the process model. Work is divided into process types (web, worker); horizontal scaling is achieved by increasing the process count.

name: Disposability
description: Maximize robustness with fast startup and graceful shutdown. Processes start in seconds and handle SIGTERM cleanly to allow zero-downtime deploys.

name: Dev / Prod Parity
description: Keep development, staging, and production as similar as possible. Minimise the time, personnel, and tool gap between environments.

name: Logs
description: Treat logs as event streams. The service writes unbuffered log lines to stdout; the execution environment routes them to the appropriate destination.

name: Admin Processes
description: Run admin/management tasks as one-off processes. Migrations, scripts, and REPL sessions run in the same environment as the production processes.

name: Availability
description: Percentage of time the service is operational and reachable. Typically expressed as an SLA (e.g. 99.9% = max 8.7 h downtime/year). Measured via uptime monitoring.

name: Response Time
description: Latency from request to response under normal load. Usually tracked as p50, p95, and p99 percentiles. Degraded response time is often the first sign of a capacity problem.

name: Throughput
description: Number of requests or transactions the service can handle per unit of time (e.g. req/s, events/min). Determines whether the service can sustain expected peak load.

name: Error Rate
description: Percentage of requests that result in an error (5xx, unhandled exceptions, timeouts). A low error rate is a primary indicator of service health and reliability.

name: Scalability
description: Ability to handle increasing load by adding resources (horizontal or vertical). Includes auto-scaling behaviour, statelessness of instances, and absence of coordination bottlenecks.

name: Recoverability
description: Speed and completeness with which the service recovers after a failure. Measured by RTO (Recovery Time Objective) and RPO (Recovery Point Objective).

name: Mean Time to Recover (MTTR)
description: Average time between a production incident being detected and the service returning to normal. A key DORA metric; lower MTTR indicates a mature incident response process.

name: Security
description: Degree to which the service protects data and resists attacks. Covers authentication, authorisation, encryption in transit and at rest, dependency vulnerability scanning, and least-privilege principles.

name: Observability
description: Ability to understand the internal state of the service from its external outputs. Requires structured logs, distributed traces, and metrics exposed to a centralised platform.

name: API Stability
description: Degree to which the public API contract is stable over time. Includes versioning strategy, backward-compatibility guarantees, and a deprecation policy for consumers.

name: Data Consistency
description: Guarantee that data remains accurate and coherent across operations and replicas. Defines the consistency model (strong, eventual) and how conflicts or partial failures are handled.

name: Test Coverage
description: Proportion of production code exercised by automated tests (unit, integration, contract). High coverage reduces regression risk; coverage alone does not guarantee quality.

name: Deployment Frequency
description: How often new versions are released to production. A key DORA metric; high frequency (multiple times per day) signals a mature CI/CD pipeline and low-risk deployments.

name: SLO Compliance
description: Percentage of time the service meets its defined Service Level Objectives. Tracks error budget consumption and triggers reliability work when the budget is close to exhausted.

name: Documentation
description: Completeness and accuracy of technical documentation: API reference (e.g. OpenAPI), runbooks, architecture decision records (ADRs), and onboarding guides.
